# Identifiers that sanitized fixtures are allowed to use in a social URL.
#
# The `no-live-accounts` check exists to stop a real account reaching apps/ or packages/.
# It cannot tell a real permalink from a fixture by looking at the URL alone, and the
# previous version tried to — by excluding any line containing the word "example". That is
# not a safety property, and the check failed on every push once the fixtures were
# sanitized, which is the worst state for a gate to be in: red for the wrong reason.
#
# So the vocabulary is enumerated instead. Adding a fixture id means adding it here, which
# is the friction that makes someone look at whether it is really synthetic.
#
# Instagram / Threads shortcodes are 11 characters; ours repeat a letter so no real code
# can collide.
DAaaaaaaaaa
DBbbbbbbbbb
DCccccccccc
DDddddddddd
# Short placeholders in unit tests that never reach a network.
/reel/ABC
/reel/AAA
/p/ABC
/p/AAA
@a/post
@x/post
@someone/post
# The permalink builder's own template, which contains no id at all.
{kind}/{code}
# LinkedIn: the synthetic activity block, plus bare counters used in parser tests.
urn:li:activity:1
urn:li:activity:100000000000000000
urn:li:ugcPost:100000000000000000
# A company page in the outbound-link test, chosen because it is a public organisation
# rather than a person.
linkedin.com/company/helsinki-nlp
# The bare host, used when asserting that a canonical URL points at LinkedIn at all.
"https://www.linkedin.com"
# Mock data marks its ids with an `example-` prefix. Allowed as a *prefix of an identifier*
# rather than as "the word example appears somewhere on the line", which is what made the
# previous filter useless.
/reel/example-
/p/example-
@example/post/
# Parser and ingest fixtures with obviously non-real ids.
/feed/update/post-
# Bare hosts inside HTML-noise fixtures, where the point is that the link carries nothing.
"https://www.linkedin.com/feed"
# The permalink builder itself, which interpolates rather than hardcoding.
${isReel(item) ? "reel" : "p"}
